reason: Nothing on disk to read, and nothing left waiting to be reviewed. Gemini's run report is one line — the intent sentence, no progress, no findings — so the wake was cut off before it wrote anything about what it read. Its two named verdict files (20261111T171835Z-a80bb862, 20261111T171837Z-70db4b53) are absent from main; both exist only on its review branch, and per the unlanded-is-not-missing rule I did not recompute them. The two items it read have since been closed by other readers anyway: a80bb862 is state=accomplished reviewer=dmitri, 70db4b53 is state=accomplished reviewer=auto:land. So a second reading of this wake would duplicate closed verdicts on evidence I cannot see. The finding that survives it, for the ledger's collection rule: a wake that produced one intent line and zero landed paths was still filed as an item worth a reviewer's turn. Collection should require at least one landed path or one line of report beyond the intent, or the queue fills with reading assignments that have no object.
